result.title: Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight
result.summary: Language models increasingly exhibit behaviors that are difficult to detect in transcripts, such as reward hacking, deception, and sycophancy. Asking the assistant follow-up questions about its actions is unreliable, since models are generally not trained to report their own misbehavior. As a result, approaches to oversight typically involve querying external models. These face limitations: external transcript monitoring operates only on visible model outputs, and activation decoders lack full context and are prone to confabulation. We introduce introspective oversight, which trains a new role in the model to answer arbitrary questions about the assistant, rewarding answers that are verified against the assistant's actual behavior. We implement this by adding a separate, third-person observer role that answers these queries, which we can train solely for accuracy and separately from the assistant. On five held-out oversight evaluations, an observer trained on Qwen3.6-27B obtains a mean AUROC of 0.907, outperforming honesty training (0.864), transcript monitoring (0.828), and activation oracles (0.796). We further find that training an observer makes the assistant itself easier to monitor, with every baseline method improving on average when applied to the fine-tuned assistant. These results suggest that training models to answer verifiable questions about themselves is a tractable approach to overseeing unintended behavior.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 introspective oversight：在模型中单独增加一个第三人称「观察者」角色，用可对照助手实际行为验证的奖励训练其回答关于助手的任意问题；在五个监督评测上平均 AUROC 0.907，优于诚实训练、转录监控与激活解码器，且经此训练后助手本身也更易被监控。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「独立训练观察者读取内部状态、并以可验证行为作奖励」的机制，可能可供核查用于检验 LVR 的 latent 状态是否真携带视觉证据、以及如何为内部推理状态设计可验证监督与贡献分配。
